The maximum is 12 hours. For more information, see Visibility Timeout in the Amazon SQS Developer Guide . For example, if the default timeout for a queue is 60 seconds, 15 seconds have…

inputFields.name: QueueUrl
inputFields.documentation: The URL of the Amazon SQS queue whose message's visibility is changed. Queue URLs and names are case-sensitive.

inputFields.name: ReceiptHandle
inputFields.documentation: The receipt handle associated with the message, whose visibility timeout is changed. This parameter is returned by the ReceiveMessage action.

inputFields.name: VisibilityTimeout
inputFields.documentation: The new value for the message's visibility timeout (in seconds). Values range: 0 to 43200 . Maximum: 12 hours.

operations.name: ChangeMessageVisibilityBatch
operations.documentation: Changes the visibility timeout of multiple messages. This is a batch version of ChangeMessageVisibility . The result of the action on each message is reported individually in the response. You can send up to 10 ChangeMessageVisibility requests with each ChangeMessageVisibilityBatch action. Because the batch request can result in a combination of successful…

inputFields.name: QueueUrl
inputFields.documentation: The URL of the Amazon SQS queue whose messages' visibility is changed. Queue URLs and names are case-sensitive.

inputFields.name: Entries
inputFields.documentation: Lists the receipt handles of the messages for which the visibility timeout must be changed.

outputFields.name: Successful
outputFields.documentation: A list of ChangeMessageVisibilityBatchResultEntry items.

outputFields.name: Failed
outputFields.documentation: A list of BatchResultErrorEntry items.

operations.name: CreateQueue
operations.documentation: Creates a new standard or FIFO queue. You can pass one or more attributes in the request. Keep the following in mind: If you don't specify the FifoQueue attribute, Amazon SQS creates a standard queue. inputFields.documentation: A map of attributes with their corresponding values. The following lists the names, descriptions, and values of the special request parameters that the CreateQueue action uses:…

outputFields.name: QueueUrl
outputFields.documentation: The URL of the created Amazon SQS queue.

operations.name: DeleteMessage
operations.documentation: Deletes the specified message from the specified queue. To select the message to delete, use the ReceiptHandle of the message ( not the MessageId which you receive when you send the message). Amazon SQS can delete a message from a queue even if a visibility timeout setting causes the message to be locked by another consumer. Amazon SQS automatically…

inputFields.name: QueueUrl
inputFields.documentation: The URL of the Amazon SQS queue from which messages are deleted. Queue URLs and names are case-sensitive.

inputFields.name: ReceiptHandle
inputFields.documentation: The receipt handle associated with the message to delete.

operations.name: DeleteMessageBatch
operations.documentation: Deletes up to ten messages from the specified queue. This is a batch version of DeleteMessage . The result of the action on each message is reported individually in the response. Because the batch request can result in a combination of successful and unsuccessful actions, you should check for batch errors even when the call returns an HTTP status code of…

inputFields.name: QueueUrl
inputFields.documentation: The URL of the Amazon SQS queue from which messages are deleted. Queue URLs and names are case-sensitive.

inputFields.name: Entries
inputFields.documentation: Lists the receipt handles for the messages to be deleted.

outputFields.name: Successful
outputFields.documentation: A list of DeleteMessageBatchResultEntry items.

outputFields.name: Failed
outputFields.documentation: A list of BatchResultErrorEntry items.

operations.name: DeleteQueue
operations.documentation: Deletes the queue specified by the QueueUrl , regardless of the queue's contents. Be careful with the DeleteQueue action: When you delete a queue, any messages in the queue are no longer available. When you delete a queue, the deletion process takes up to 60 seconds. Requests you send involving that queue during the 60 seconds might succeed. For example, a…

inputFields.name: QueueUrl
inputFields.documentation: The URL of the Amazon SQS queue to delete. Queue URLs and names are case-sensitive.

operations.name: GetQueueAttributes
operations.documentation: Gets attributes for the specified queue. To determine whether a queue is FIFO , you can check whether QueueName ends with the .fifo suffix.

inputFields.name: QueueUrl
inputFields.documentation: The URL of the Amazon SQS queue whose attribute information is retrieved. Queue URLs and names are case-sensitive.

inputFields.name: AttributeNames
inputFields.documentation: A list of attributes for which to retrieve information. The AttributeNames parameter is optional, but if you don't specify values for this parameter, the request returns empty…

outputFields.name: Attributes
outputFields.documentation: A map of attributes to their respective values.

operations.name: GetQueueUrl
operations.documentation: The GetQueueUrl API returns the URL of an existing Amazon SQS queue. This is useful when you know the queue's name but need to retrieve its URL for further operations. inputFields.documentation: (Optional) The Amazon Web Services account ID of the account that created the queue. This is only required when you are attempting to access a queue owned by another Amazon Web…

outputFields.name: QueueUrl
outputFields.documentation: The URL of the queue.

operations.name: ListDeadLetterSourceQueues
operations.documentation: Returns a list of your queues that have the RedrivePolicy queue attribute configured with a dead-letter queue. The ListDeadLetterSourceQueues methods supports pagination. Set parameter MaxResults in the request to specify the maximum number of results to be returned in the response. If you do not set MaxResults , the response includes a maximum of 1,000…

inputFields.name: QueueUrl
inputFields.documentation: The URL of a dead-letter queue. Queue URLs and names are case-sensitive.

inputFields.name: NextToken
inputFields.documentation: Pagination token to request the next set of results.

inputFields.name: MaxResults
inputFields.documentation: Maximum number of results to include in the response. Value range is 1 to 1000. You must set MaxResults to receive a value for NextToken in the response.

outputFields.name: queueUrls
outputFields.documentation: A list of source queue URLs that have the RedrivePolicy queue attribute configured with a dead-letter queue.

outputFields.name: NextToken
outputFields.documentation: Pagination token to include in the next request. Token value is null if there are no additional results to request, or if you did not set MaxResults in the request.

operations.name: ListMessageMoveTasks
operations.documentation: Gets the most recent message movement tasks (up to 10) under a specific source queue. This action is currently limited to supporting message redrive from dead-letter queues (DLQs) only. inputFields.name: SourceArn
inputFields.documentation: The ARN of the queue whose message movement tasks are to be listed.

inputFields.name: MaxResults
inputFields.documentation: The maximum number of results to include in the response. The default is 1, which provides the most recent message movement task. The upper limit is 10.

outputFields.name: Results
outputFields.documentation: A list of message movement tasks and their attributes.

operations.name: ListQueues
operations.documentation: Returns a list of your queues in the current region. The response includes a maximum of 1,000 results. If you specify a value for the optional QueueNamePrefix parameter, only queues with a name that begins with the specified value are returned. The listQueues methods supports pagination. inputFields.name: QueueNamePrefix
inputFields.documentation: A string to use for filtering the list results. Only those queues whose name begins with the specified string are returned. Queue URLs and names are case-sensitive.

inputFields.name: NextToken
inputFields.documentation: Pagination token to request the next set of results.

inputFields.name: MaxResults
inputFields.documentation: Maximum number of results to include in the response. Value range is 1 to 1000. You must set MaxResults to receive a value for NextToken in the response.

outputFields.name: QueueUrls
outputFields.documentation: A list of queue URLs, up to 1,000 entries, or the value of MaxResults that you sent in the request.

outputFields.name: NextToken
outputFields.documentation: Pagination token to include in the next request. Token value is null if there are no additional results to request, or if you did not set MaxResults in the request.

operations.name: ListQueueTags
operations.documentation: List all cost allocation tags added to the specified Amazon SQS queue. For an overview, see Tagging Your Amazon SQS Queues in the Amazon SQS Developer Guide . Cross-account permissions don't apply to this action. For more information, see Grant cross-account permissions to a role and a username in the Amazon SQS Developer Guide .

inputFields.name: QueueUrl
inputFields.documentation: The URL of the queue.

outputFields.name: Tags
outputFields.documentation: The list of all tags added to the specified queue.

operations.name: PurgeQueue
operations.documentation: Deletes available messages in a queue (including in-flight messages) specified by the QueueURL parameter. We recommend waiting for 60 seconds regardless of your queue's size. Messages sent to the queue before you…

inputFields.name: QueueUrl
inputFields.documentation: The URL of the queue from which the PurgeQueue action deletes messages. Queue URLs and names are case-sensitive.

operations.name: ReceiveMessage
operations.documentation: Retrieves one or more messages (up to 10), from the specified queue. Using the WaitTimeSeconds parameter enables long-poll support. inputFields.documentation: The maximum number of messages to return. Amazon SQS never returns more messages than this value (however, fewer messages might be returned). Valid values: 1 to 10. Default: 1.

operations.name: RemovePermission
operations.documentation: Revokes any permissions in the queue policy that matches the specified Label parameter. Only the owner of a queue can remove permissions from it. inputFields.documentation: The URL of the Amazon SQS queue from which permissions are removed. Queue URLs and names are case-sensitive.

inputFields.documentation: The identification of the permission to remove. This is the label added using the AddPermission action.

inputFields.name: MessageAttributes
inputFields.documentation: Each message attribute consists of a Name , Type , and Value . For more information, see Amazon SQS message attributes in the Amazon SQS Developer Guide .

operations.name: SendMessageBatch
operations.documentation: You can use SendMessageBatch to send up to 10 messages to the specified queue by assigning either identical or different values to each message (or by not assigning values at all). inputFields.documentation: The URL of the Amazon SQS queue to which batched messages are sent. Queue URLs and names are case-sensitive.

inputFields.name: Entries

operations.name: SetQueueAttributes
operations.documentation: Sets the value of one or more queue attributes, like a policy. operations.name: StartMessageMoveTask
operations.documentation: Starts an asynchronous task to move messages from a specified source queue to a specified destination queue. This action is currently limited to supporting message redrive from queues that are configured as dead-letter queues (DLQs) of other Amazon SQS queues only. operations.name: TagQueue
operations.documentation: Add cost allocation tags to the specified Amazon SQS queue. For an overview, see Tagging Your Amazon SQS Queues in the Amazon SQS Developer Guide . operations.name: UntagQueue
operations.documentation: Remove cost allocation tags from the specified Amazon SQS queue. For an overview, see Tagging Your Amazon SQS Queues in the Amazon SQS Developer Guide . Cross-account permissions don't apply to this action. For more information, see Grant cross-account permissions to a role and a username in the Amazon SQS Developer Guide .
